lessons.title: Clearance is a design input
lessons.teach: A 0.4 mm Bambu nozzle cannot hold CNC fits. Model +0.40 mm diametral clearance in CAD for every printed-to-printed running or slip interface (journal/bushing, posts/top plate, bushing/seat). Leave slicer XY hole compensation at 0 unless a gauge print says otherwise.

lessons.title: No FDM press fits
lessons.teach: Press fits fail from elephant foot and shrinkage. Use +0.40 slip and retain with a shoulder, cone, plate, or cap. Do not assume a metal bearing will appear later.

lessons.title: Build the assembled stack
lessons.teach: The exam is a mechanism, not a print-bed scatter. Place bodies on one axis in assembly order: shaft cone in the base cup, rotor on the shoulder, top plate on the three posts, printed bushing in the plate, cap on the journal. noBS CAD has no mates or assembly configs — this placement is manual and that gap is the point.

lessons.title: Print a thrust bearing contour
lessons.teach: A 45° cone-in-cup is an easy-to-rotate printed thrust. The shaft tip is lifted so it seats on the cone face, not the point. A small relief hole under the apex keeps the tip from bottoming.

lessons.title: Keep the machine even
lessons.teach: Three posts at 120° and two rotor buckets at 180° so the spinner is balanced around the axis. An odd one-sided vane will not run true.

lessons.title: Print the bearings too
lessons.teach: This kit is fully printable: conical thrust plus a printed sleeve bushing. Metal 608 / catalog bearings are a later option from a standard table, not a hidden part of the exam.

lessons.title: The rotor is a part that mounts
lessons.teach: A lone C-loft coupon is not a rotor. The even spinner has a hub that slips onto the shaft and two helical buckets joined to that hub.

lessons.title: Export a printable package
lessons.teach: Assign appearances, run solid_export_preflight, then solid_export_3mf for bambu_studio. Print each body in its own orientation (base/plate flat, shaft on the cone, bushing as a ring, rotor on the hub face). 3MF is the manufacturing handoff.
